anomalies.observed: U1's EN pin 2 is marked no-connect, leaving the TPS62933 buck regulator disabled rather than enabling it.
anomalies.expected: EN should be connected to an enabling signal or supply so the regulator can generate the +5V rail described in the specification.

evidence.quote: U1 TPS62933, pin 2 EN marked no-connect; sheet /, page 1.

anomalies.impact: The +5V rail may not come up, preventing the ESP32 DevKit and downstream 3.3V regulator from being powered as intended.

anomalies.observed: T5's gate node G_ATO is pulled to GND by R12 (10k) and connected to T4's collector. T4's emitter is grounded, while ATO_VALVE and FLOAT_HIGH drive its base through R10 and R11. There is no path that drives T5's gate high.
anomalies.expected: The ATO valve low-side switch must be able to drive its MOSFET gate high to turn the valve on, while allowing the control and float-switch signals to disable it.

evidence.quote: T5 AO3400A gate at G_ATO; R12 10k to GND; T4 BT3904 emitter to GND; sheet /, page 1.
T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch

anomalies.impact: The ATO valve MOSFET gate remains low, so the valve cannot be switched on by the shown control circuit.

anomalies.observed: T2's gate node G_PUMP is pulled up to +3V3 by R5 (10k), while T1's grounded-emitter NPN can pull that node low when driven from PUMP_MAIN. Thus the main-pump MOSFET is on when the control is inactive and off when the NPN is driven.
anomalies.expected: The main-pump switch should default to off when its controller is inactive or resetting, and its control should turn the pump on rather than pull the MOSFET gate low.

evidence.quote: R5 10k from +3V3 to G_PUMP; T1 BT3904 emitter to GND; T2 IRLR2905 gate at G_PUMP; sheet /, page 1.
T2 — IRLR2905 (DPAK N-MOSFET) | Main circulation-pump low-side switch

anomalies.impact: The main circulation pump is liable to run when the controller is unpowered, resetting, or not actively asserting its control, and the control polarity is inverted.

parsed.summary: The drawing shows the buck regulator's enable pin left disconnected, an ATO MOSFET gate that has no means of being driven high, and a main-pump MOSFET that defaults on with inverted control. These deviations can prevent expected power-up and actuator behavior.
